caveats.injuries: Injury report from the league's official practice reports via nflverse: shown, not applied. The model reads only who starts at quarterback.
caveats.lines: Model line and model total are the model's own numbers beside the market's. Taking the model's side against the closing spread won 49.8% of 2016-2025 games and against the total 50.1%; -110 needs 52.4% to break even.
caveats.model: The pick is the model blended with the betting market. The market is hard to beat in the NFL: across 2016-2025 the blend picked 66.4% of winners against the closing favourite's 66.6%, and betting the model where it disagreed with the price lost money. Treat a pick as an opinion with a measured hit rate, not an edge.
caveats.news: Headlines from public NFL news feeds that name one of the two teams or their players, published before kickoff. Shown, not applied.
caveats.players: Most valuable on offence is ranked by expected points added (EPA) this season - the points a player's plays added above an average play in the same situation; defenders by sacks, takeaways, passes defended and tackles for loss. A listed player who is out or doubtful - or the most valuable player questionable - is flagged at the top of the game, from the official injury report and the weekly roster. Shown, not applied: only the starting quarterback moves the pick.
caveats.props: Projected yards are the middle of what the player's recent usage and his team's expected points point to, if he plays. In 2020-2025: passing 56 yards off on average (his own average: 67); rushing 18 yards off on average (his own average: 18); receiving 18 yards off on average (his own average: 20). Players went over about half the time, as a middle number should. Shown, not applied.
caveats.qb: The quarterback the model assumes is the one the schedule projects to start. If the injury report says he is out, the number above does not know yet.
caveats.td: Chance of a rushing or receiving touchdown, if he plays - from his recent carries, targets and snaps and his team's expected points from the betting line. In 2020-2025 each team's most likely scorer scored 43.5% of the time (the model said 41.1%). Measured, and shown, not applied.
caveats.td_list: Every active QB, RB, FB, WR and TE is listed - everyone you can back to score. A chance is shown only where the model was measured as well calibrated: within 20% of what happened in both 2014-2019 and 2020-2025. Players with little use or no NFL game are listed with a dash instead. For players with no NFL game: it said 2.7% where 7.9% scored (2020-2025); under 0.5 weighted carries + targets a game: it said 3.7% where 2.7% scored (2020-2025); 0.5-1 weighted carries + targets a game: it said 6.2% where 4.9% scored (2014-2019).
caveats.td_meters: Two meters from the live record - touchdown picks logged before kickoff, games graded from the box score. TOP 3 -> SCORED: of the times a player was in his team's top three most likely touchdown scorers, how often he scored a rushing or receiving touchdown; a pick who did not play is left out, as every chance was if he plays. NOT TOP 3 -> NO TD: of the times a player played without being in that top three, how often he did not score. Where the whole list a bettor could back (every active QB, RB, FB, WR and TE) was logged before kickoff, 'not top 3' is the rest of that list who played. Games logged before that list was, with only the top three, rebuild 'not top 3' from the snap counts: every other player of the team who took an offensive snap at QB, RB, FB, WR or TE, his touchdowns from the box score (none if he has no box-score line).
caveats.td_odds: Anytime-TD odds are the books' consensus Yes price (the-odds-api, US books), not Stake's: est. The implied chance beside it is 1 / that price with the books' margin left in, so it reads above the books' own fair chance - a Yes-only price cannot be de-vigged. The touchdown model's chance has never been measured against these prices (no past anytime-TD price is on file), so a gap between the two is not an edge.
caveats.tiers: STRONG, SOLID, LEAN and TOSS-UP are bands of the pick's probability. The percentage beside each is how often picks in that band won in 2016-2025 - measured, not promised.
caveats.value_off: No game is labelled a bet: backing the model where it disagreed with the closing moneyline did not make money in 2016-2025 at any edge tested.

caveats.bias: In the backtest a TD candidate is a player who took a snap, so the replay knows who was active. Live, a pick who does not play is voided and the ticket is graded on its other legs.
caveats.chance: The chance is the product of the legs' chances - what the ticket would hit if its legs were independent. Legs in one game are not (a team winning and its running back scoring go together), so the backtest measures how often each kind actually hit beside this product, and both are shown.
caveats.edge: Nothing here claims an edge. The market is hard to beat, and parlays multiply the margin of every leg; these tickets are the legs the engine rates most likely to land, not bets it rates profitable.
caveats.edge_v2: Nothing here claims an edge. Narrowing to likely legs raises the hit rate and lowers the payout; the market prices both. These are the legs the engine rates most likely to land, not bets it rates profitable.
caveats.est: est. - the product of the legs' consensus single prices; Stake's bet builder prices correlated legs below it, so it is an upper bound on what Stake pays
caveats.est_erratum: Correction, found after the rule was fixed: the est. payout is not an upper bound. A bet builder prices legs that go together below the product of the singles, but can price legs that pull against each other above it (a touchdown on one team beside the other team's result, or beside the under), and Stake's single prices are not the books' consensus - so the est. payout, and the live return read at it, is an estimate that Stake's quote can beat or fall short of.
caveats.exact: The exact payout is the price Stake quotes for the slip: enter it as typed and the return on the stake is worked out from it.

legs.SPREAD: a team at the posted spread; chance: the market's no-vig at the consensus spread prices, since the model does not beat the line; a push voids the leg
legs.TD: a player scores 1+ rushing or receiving touchdown, overtime included - passing, return and fumble-recovery touchdowns do not count; chance: the touchdown model's, if he plays, only where his usage group was measured as calibrated; a player who does not play voids the leg
legs.TOTAL: over or under the posted game total; chance: the market's no-vig at the consensus total prices; a push voids the leg
legs.WIN: a team to win, overtime included; chance: the pick's blend; a tie voids the leg

caveats.live: Live: every ticket logged before kickoff, graded from the box score, its return at the logged est. payout - so an upper bound, and marked so.
caveats.meters: Each kind is metered on its own, as if $10 had been bet on every ticket of that kind: hit rate is won / (won + lost), beside the mean product chance of the same tickets.
caveats.not_in_v1: Not in v1, because nothing on file measures them yet: QB pass attempts, yards over a line, first/second-half points, team or game touchdown totals, alternate ("Asian") lines.
caveats.objective: the highest SMALL hit rate (won / (won + lost)) among the pairs that build a SMALL ticket in at least 25% of 2014-2019's games; ties to the larger coverage, then the lower CONFIDENT, then the lower TD_FLOOR
caveats.prices: Every price is the books' consensus single price, not Stake's: an estimate, marked est.
caveats.roi_priced: The return is over the graded tickets that had every leg's price; a ticket with a leg the books had not priced is counted in the hit rate but not in the return.
caveats.rookie: A ROOKIE leg is a TD leg on a player in his first NFL season: no game in player_games in any earlier season.

rules.chosen: 65% and 45% were chosen on 2014-2019 only, by the highest SMALL hit rate (won / (won + lost)) among the pairs that build a SMALL ticket in at least 25% of 2014-2019's games; ties to the larger coverage, then the lower CONFIDENT, then the lower TD_FLOOR; measured untouched on 2020-2025 and the current season
rules.games: only a confident game gets tickets: the pick's chance is 65% or more; every other game shows no tickets, and why
rules.result: result legs only on the pick's side: the pick's WIN and the pick's SPREAD
rules.small: the pick's best TD scorer: the best TD leg on the pick's team at 45% or more, else the game's best that clears it, + the best result leg on the pick's side
rules.td: only players the model rates very likely: a TD chance of 45% or more (the rookie leg keeps v1's 25% and must be on the pick's team)
rules.total: unchanged from v1 (the market's no-vig side): MEDIUM's third slot competes with the TD legs, LARGE's fourth slot is a total

caveats.slots: Built in the order SMALL, ROOKIE, MEDIUM, LARGE, each slot taking the highest-chance leg still available: a leg is in at most 2 of a game's 4 tickets. A slot with nothing available leaves its ticket unbuilt, with the reason.

tickets.large: the best TD at 45% or more + the next-best TD at 45% or more (another player) + the best result leg on the pick's side (its WIN or SPREAD) + the best TOTAL leg
tickets.medium: the best TD at 45% or more + the best result leg on the pick's side (its WIN or SPREAD) + the best of the TOTAL legs and the TD legs at 45% or more on other players
tickets.rookie: the best rookie TD on the pick's team with a chance of 25% or more + the pick's WIN
tickets.small: the pick's best TD scorer - the best TD at 45% or more on the pick's team, else the game's best at 45% or more - + the best result leg on the pick's side (its WIN or SPREAD)

caveats.untouched: Untouched means the two numbers: they were chosen on 2014-2019 alone. SMALL's taking the pick's own team's scorer first is a clause of the rule, motivated by a 2016-2025 statistic (how often a player scored when his team won against when it lost, the research before v1), so for that clause 2020-2025 is not a clean holdout; SMALL with the game's best TD, beside it, is the comparison that shows the clause's effect.

chosen.objective: the highest SMALL hit rate (won / (won + lost)) among the pairs that build a SMALL ticket in at least 25% of 2014-2019's games; ties to the larger coverage, then the lower CONFIDENT, then the lower TD_FLOOR

rises.claim: Hit rate always rises as the bars rise
rises.note: Found after the rule was fixed: the rule's words say "Hit rate always rises as the bars rise", but on 2014-2019 SMALL's hit rate fell at 6 of the grid's 24 steps (one bar raised a step, the other held). The choice does not rest on that sentence: the objective takes the best hit rate among the pairs that clear the coverage floor (25%). The floor did stop the choice: without it the best would be 70% and 50%, which hit 47.9% but was built in 14.7% of the games.

chosen.untouched: Untouched means the two numbers: they were chosen on 2014-2019 alone. SMALL's taking the pick's own team's scorer first is a clause of the rule, motivated by a 2016-2025 statistic (how often a player scored when his team won against when it lost, the research before v1), so for that clause 2020-2025 is not a clean holdout; SMALL with the game's best TD, beside it, is the comparison that shows the clause's effect.

grid.note: every pair of the grid, per period; only the DEV figures chose, and only by the objective

caveats.bias: In the backtest a TD candidate is a player who took a snap, so the replay knows who was active. Live, a pick who does not play is voided and the ticket is graded on its other legs.
caveats.chance: The chance is the product of the legs' chances - what the ticket would hit if its legs were independent. Legs in one game are not (a team winning and its running back scoring go together), so the backtest measures how often each kind actually hit beside this product, and both are shown.
caveats.edge: Nothing here claims an edge. The market is hard to beat, and parlays multiply the margin of every leg; these tickets are the legs the engine rates most likely to land, not bets it rates profitable.
caveats.est: est. - the product of the legs' consensus single prices; Stake's bet builder prices correlated legs below it, so it is an upper bound on what Stake pays
caveats.est_erratum: Correction, found after the rule was fixed: the est. payout is not an upper bound. A bet builder prices legs that go together below the product of the singles, but can price legs that pull against each other above it (a touchdown on one team beside the other team's result, or beside the under), and Stake's single prices are not the books' consensus - so the est. payout, and the live return read at it, is an estimate that Stake's quote can beat or fall short of.
caveats.exact: The exact payout is the price Stake quotes for the slip: enter it as typed and the return on the stake is worked out from it.

legs.SPREAD: a team at the posted spread; chance: the market's no-vig at the consensus spread prices, since the model does not beat the line; a push voids the leg
legs.TD: a player scores 1+ rushing or receiving touchdown, overtime included - passing, return and fumble-recovery touchdowns do not count; chance: the touchdown model's, if he plays, only where his usage group was measured as calibrated; a player who does not play voids the leg
legs.TOTAL: over or under the posted game total; chance: the market's no-vig at the consensus total prices; a push voids the leg
legs.WIN: a team to win, overtime included; chance: the pick's blend; a tie voids the leg

caveats.live: Live: every ticket logged before kickoff, graded from the box score, its return at the logged est. payout - so an upper bound, and marked so.
caveats.meters: Each kind is metered on its own, as if $10 had been bet on every ticket of that kind: hit rate is won / (won + lost), beside the mean product chance of the same tickets.
caveats.not_in_v1: Not in v1, because nothing on file measures them yet: QB pass attempts, yards over a line, first/second-half points, team or game touchdown totals, alternate ("Asian") lines.
caveats.prices: Every price is the books' consensus single price, not Stake's: an estimate, marked est.
caveats.roi_priced: The return is over the graded tickets that had every leg's price; a ticket with a leg the books had not priced is counted in the hit rate but not in the return.
caveats.rookie: A ROOKIE leg is a TD leg on a player in his first NFL season: no game in player_games in any earlier season.
caveats.slots: Built in the order SMALL, ROOKIE, MEDIUM, LARGE, each slot taking the highest-chance leg still available: a leg is in at most 2 of a game's 4 tickets. A slot with nothing available leaves its ticket unbuilt, with the reason.

tickets.large: the best TD + the next-best TD (another player) + the best result leg + the best TOTAL leg
tickets.medium: the best TD + the best result leg + the best of the TOTAL legs and the TD legs on other players
tickets.rookie: the best rookie TD with a chance of 25% or more + WIN for the rookie's own team
tickets.small: the best TD + the best result leg (WIN or SPREAD)
